sentences.text: Abavornis is a bird-like creature tentatively placed within the Enantiornithes, a group of early birds known for their unique wing structures.
Currently, only one species, A. bonaparti, is recognized within this genus.
The type fossil was discovered in the Bissekty Formation located in the Kyzylkum region of Uzbekistan.
A second partial coracoid fossil, labeled Abavornis sp., resembles the type specimen and might reveal damaged features of the holotype.
The species name bonaparti honors the Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte.
Taxonomically, Abavornis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
It is further classified within the parent group Alexornithidae.
This animal lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
